## The eddy-diffusion tendency of a column (`diffusion_tendency`) {#sec-ch08-tendency}

### Summary

This scheme returns the rate of change of every species at every level caused by eddy diffusion. It applies the
coefficients of @sec-ch08-operator to the profiles. A caller adds the result to its other tendencies, or uses the
same coefficients to build an implicit matrix, and takes the time step itself.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $\mathrm d y / \mathrm d t$ from @eq-ch08-operator-tendency for all levels and species.

**Data.** `y` (levels, species), `Kzz` and `dzi` (faces); returns the same shape as `y`.

**Placement.** A spatial tendency; the caller owns the time integration.

**Activation.** Always available; Python `kintera.diffusion_tendency`.

**Guarantee / limits.** As @sec-ch08-operator; explicit stepping needs a small step.

**Evidence.** `test_diffusion`, `test_atm2d.py`; see the Tests layer.
:::

The symbols are those of @sec-ch08-operator. The scheme has no option and no default.

### Derivation

No derivation beyond @sec-ch08-operator: the tendency is @eq-ch08-operator-tendency evaluated with the
coefficients of @eq-ch08-operator-inner and @eq-ch08-operator-boundary.

### Numerical method

The tendency starts as $A_j\, y_{j,s}$ for every level. Then $B_j\, y_{j+1,s}$ is added on levels $0$ to $N-2$, and
$C_j\, y_{j-1,s}$ on levels $1$ to $N-1$. The coefficients are broadcast over the species dimension. The result is
exact to rounding for the operator; the caller's time scheme sets the accuracy in time. The stability limit of an
explicit step is not derived here. The test below uses a forward-Euler step of $0.1\, h^2/K$.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| tendency | {{< code src/diffusion/diffusion.cpp diffusion_tendency >}} | `diffusion_tendency` | always |
| declaration | {{< code src/diffusion/diffusion.hpp diffusion_tendency >}} | `diffusion_tendency` | always |
| Python binding | {{< code python/csrc/pydiffusion.cpp bind_diffusion >}} | `bind_diffusion` | always |

: Code map of the eddy-diffusion tendency. {#tbl-ch08-tendency-code}

1. `diffusion_tendency` calls `diffusion_coefficients` and adds a trailing dimension to the three coefficient
   vectors $A$, $B$ and $C$.
2. It forms `A * y`, then adds the upper and lower neighbour terms in place on slices.
3. `bind_diffusion` exposes both functions to Python as `kintera.diffusion_tendency(y, Kzz, dzi)` and
   `kintera.diffusion_coefficients(y, Kzz, dzi)`, with the same argument names.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_diffusion` | `TendencyShape`: output is (levels, species) | exact | structural |
| `test_diffusion` | `TendencySignCorrect`: negative at the peak, positive near the edge | sign only | the test |
| `test_diffusion` | `GaussianSmooths`: 100 Euler steps lower the peak by over 5% | peak ratio below 0.95 | the test |
| `test_diffusion` | `GaussianSmooths`: total of species 0 kept within 1% | relative 0.01 | the test, after clamping at zero |
| `test_atm2d.py` | the 2-D eddy matrix equals this tendency per column | rtol and atol $10^{-12}$ | `assert_close` arguments |

: Tests of the eddy-diffusion tendency. {#tbl-ch08-tendency-tests}

The C++ cases are in {{< code tests/test_diffusion.cpp >}}, on the uniform 20-level grid of @sec-ch08-operator, in
float64 on CPU and CUDA. The Python case is `test_vertical_eddy_transport_matches_columnwise_reference`
({{< code tests/test_atm2d.py test_vertical_eddy_transport_matches_columnwise_reference >}}). It builds the
two-dimensional eddy matrix of @sec-ch09 for two columns of five levels, with face coefficients taken as the mean of
the centre values. It then compares each column with this function at $10^{-12}$. This draft has not run the tests
and attaches no run record (missing evidence).

### Limits

- The Gaussian test clamps negative values to zero after each step, so its 1% conservation bound includes the
  clamp; @prp-ch08-operator-column-total is the exact statement.
- Only float64 is instantiated in `test_diffusion`; float32 is not tested.
- Molecular diffusion is not provided here: `src/diffusion` has only the eddy term. The binary (molecular)
  diffusion matrix is built in the two-dimensional solver
  ({{< code python/atm2d/transport.py build_binary_diffusion_matrix >}}); answered at @sec-ch09-molecular.
